scenarios.title: Team Under Pressure
scenarios.scenario: Your team is burning out the day before a major project deadline. Half the members are overwhelmed, one person is threatening to quit, and the client is demanding deliverables. You are the team lead.
options: Push through the night yourself — take on the weakest members' tasks and deliver on time at any cost.
Call the client immediately, renegotiate the deadline honestly, and protect your team's wellbeing.
Hold a 15-minute emergency standup: redistribute workload, define a minimal viable deliverable, ship it.
Let each person decide their own workload — don't interfere, trust the team's self-organization.

scenarios.title: Hidden Misconduct
scenarios.scenario: You discover a colleague has been falsifying progress reports to avoid conflict. Leadership believes the project is on track, but it's actually 3 weeks behind. The colleague is your friend.
options: Report to leadership immediately — transparency is non-negotiable regardless of personal cost.
Talk to the colleague privately first: give them 48 hours to come clean themselves.
Work with the colleague to rapidly close the gap, then jointly disclose the situation to leadership.
Fix it quietly — cover the gap yourself, ensure delivery, and never mention it happened.

scenarios.title: Resource Constraint
scenarios.scenario: You are leading a community project with a fixed budget. A team member proposes an idea that could genuinely transform outcomes — but it requires 3 extra weeks of work and 40% more budget than allocated.
options: Decline the idea — constraints exist for a reason, stick to the original plan.
Build a quick prototype to validate the idea in 3 days, then present evidence to renegotiate resources.
Find creative ways to implement a simplified version of the idea within current constraints.
Bring the full proposal to stakeholders with a ROI argument and request additional resources formally.

scenarios.title: Conflicting Priorities
scenarios.scenario: Two stakeholders you report to want opposite things for the same deadline: one demands speed and a rough launch, the other insists on polish and zero known bugs. Neither will budge in writing.
options: Deliver to the more senior stakeholder and apologize later to the other.
Schedule a joint 30-minute alignment with both, document a written trade-off decision, then execute.
Split the team in two and try to satisfy both in parallel without telling them.
Delay both slightly and build quietly until you can meet the higher quality bar.

scenarios.title: Chronic Under-Delivery
scenarios.scenario: A capable teammate keeps missing internal deadlines. Others compensate, resentment is growing, and the person says they are overwhelmed but rejects help.
options: Escalate to HR immediately for performance review.
Have a direct 1:1: name the pattern, ask what would help, agree on smaller commitments with checkpoints.
Reassign their critical tasks without discussion to protect the team timeline.
Ignore it — confronting peers might damage psychological safety.

scenarios.title: Ethical Grey Area
scenarios.scenario: A client asks you to omit a limitation from a public summary so the pitch looks stronger. It is not illegal, but it could mislead end users. Your bonus depends partly on client satisfaction.
options: Refuse and offer a truthful reframing that still highlights strengths.
Comply quietly — everyone rounds corners in competitive markets.
Ask legal/compliance in writing and do nothing until you have a written ruling.
Leak the concern anonymously so the client backs off without tracing it to you.
